faq.q: How many mobile home parks does this page list?
faq.a: 73 entries in page order, covering Abbotsford, Agassiz/Kent, Chilliwack, Coquitlam, Cultus Lake, Soowahlie, Hope, Langley, Maple Ridge, Mission, Rosedale, Ruskin and Surrey — with Cedar Grove and Mountainview Estates in Chilliwack each listed twice, so the distinct count is lower, and the list is site copy only because no official park registry exists.

faq.q: What happens if the park is sold or converted to another use?
faq.a: Under MHPTA s.42 the landlord must first have all required government permits and approvals, give 12 months' notice, and pay $20,000 on or before the effective date; the tenant may leave early on 10 days' notice, has 15 days to dispute, and may be eligible for additional compensation of the assessed value minus $20,000 through dispute resolution.

faq.q: Are there market statistics for Fraser Valley mobile homes?
faq.a: No — SnapStats has no manufactured-home category. The only figures in this file are all-residential community context as of September 2026 (Source: SnapStats FVR September 2026 report), for example Langley Detached median $1,345,000 and Condos & Townhomes median $611,000, and neither describes park homes (SnapStats FVR September 2026 report, read 2026-11-01).

faq.q: Do I own the land under a mobile home in Fraser Valley?
faq.a: Usually not. In most parks you own the home and pay monthly pad rent to the park owner, and the tenancy falls under BC's Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act. Ask for the tenancy agreement, the current pad rent and the park rules before you make an offer.

faq.q: Can I get a mortgage on a mobile home in Fraser Valley?
faq.a: Lenders look at the age of the home, whether it carries a CSA certification label and the terms of the pad tenancy, and some will not finance older homes. Speak to a mortgage broker before you write an offer, not after.
